Hi Laura / Marcus,

I'm writing to request HR guidance and a quick review of a pre-PIP coaching approach for Samir Khan (Platform Engineer, Team: Infra Foundations). Over the last two months we've seen:
- consistently missed sprint commitments (avg 40% of committed work incomplete),
- multiple post-release bugs traced to his modules (3 high-severity escapes in Jan–Feb),
- PR turnaround times >7 days which is blocking peers.

I don't think we're at formal PIP yet; my intent is a documented, time-boxed "stabilization" (coaching) plan with clear metrics and supports. I've attached a draft outline for a 6-week plan that includes:
- specific, measurable targets (PR turn-around <=48 hrs, reduce bug escapes to <2% per sprint),
- weekly 1:1 check-ins + pairing sessions,
- a mentor assignment and recommended trainings,
- milestones for calibration at weeks 3 and 6.

Request: can HR review the attached and confirm (a) this is framed correctly as pre-PIP coaching, (b) any required wording or documentation we should include, and (c) any recordkeeping steps I should complete before I present this to Samir? Also advise whether Monica should be present for the initial conversation.

Thanks for the heads-up, Hannah. Appreciate the draft — good baseline. A few quick HR notes: 

1) Frame and tone: call it a "Performance Stabilization Plan (informal coaching track)" — avoid language like "final warning" or "immediate PIP" unless you've exhausted coaching and have legal/HR sign-off.

2) Metrics & evidence: HR wants the targets to be measurable and tied to time windows (e.g., PR merge within 48 hours across next 2 sprints). Include baseline numbers and the data source for them.

3) Support: document offered supports (mentor pairing, training sessions, reasonable accommodation if relevant). Make sure Samir has a chance to commit to concrete actions.

4) Timeline: 6–8 weeks is typical for stabilization; indicate when you'll do a mid-point calibration (week 3 or 4).

5) Recordkeeping: Save meeting notes in the HR case (file HR-4521) and share the plan with Samir at the start of the coaching period. HR will create the personnel record once you send the finalized plan.

If you want, I can review the updated draft language and sign off. No need to loop external counsel yet — we involve them only if the plan escalates to a formal PIP/termination track.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. People Business Partner (Engineering)
Redwood Inference
